title: Transition to operations
blurb: Plan a hand-over that keeps agile practices alive: artifacts and tools, training, procedures, escalation pathways and feedback loops.
question: Draycott Precision Engineering's maintenance team will own the predictive dashboard after the project. What should be handed over so the team keeps working in an agile way, and how will it learn what to improve?

teach.h: A hand-over that keeps agility alive
teach.body: When an agile project's products move into operational use, PRINCE2 Agile guidance aims for continuity: the people running the product should keep the agile practices that built it, adopt the product quickly, maintain it consistently and keep learning. Transition is planned early and happens release by release, not only at the end. The guidance covers agile artifacts and tools, end-user training, operational procedures, escalation pathways and feedback loops.

head: Element
Examples
What it achieves
rows: Backlogs, dashboards, the tools behind them
Continuity with agile practices after hand-over
Tailored sessions, manuals, quick-start guides, videos
Step-by-step configuration management, maintenance schedules, SLAs, troubleshooting
Points of contact and timelines for resolving issues

teach.h: Planned early, confirmed at the end
teach.body: Transition is not a last-minute task. In initiation, 'prepare the project plan' identifies how the project product will move into operational use. During stages, the PM confirms in 'evaluate stage status' whether ownership of released products has passed to users. In closing, 'confirm project acceptance' checks from the PID how products are delivered to operations, and the closure workshop's 'final handover planning' sets support responsibilities, operational requirements and benefits actions.

items.label: Release 1: pilot estate reporting to contact centre
Release 2: diagnosis guide and parts list to repairs
Release 3: all homes; final hand-over at closure

teach.h: Worked scenario: Saltmarsh Housing Group's Repairs Reimagined
teach.body: Sally Greaves planned transition in initiation. For Release 2, contact centre advisers get short training, a quick-start card and videos for the diagnosis guide. The repairs team receives step-by-step procedures and an escalation path to Coastline with response times. The service design team hands its Kanban board and dashboard to the repairs team so improvement continues. Monthly tenant surveys and adviser check-ins feed the backlog, and Sally confirms each ownership transfer when she evaluates stage status.

teach.text: Traps: quick-start guides and manuals aid adoption; they do not collect insight. SLAs and maintenance schedules set operational expectations; they are not feedback loops. Escalation pathways say who to contact and how fast. It is the handed-over agile artifacts and tools that keep agile practices going after transition.

items: Hand over agile artifacts and tools for continuity of agile practices.
Tailored training, manuals, quick-start guides and videos drive adoption.
Explicit procedures: configuration, maintenance schedules, SLAs, troubleshooting.
Escalation pathways: contacts and timelines for resolving issues.
Feedback loops (surveys, retrospectives, check-ins) give actionable insight.

summary: You can now plan a transition to operations that keeps agile practices alive, choosing the right element for each need. You can also say where transition is planned and confirmed across the processes.

A.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group's Release 2 gives contact centre advisers a new diagnosis guide. Joy Ansah, the contact centre manager, wants her 28 advisers using it confidently from day one. Which transition step BEST supports this?
options: Tailored training with quick-start guides and short videos
A service level agreement with Coastline on response times
A monthly survey of tenants about their repair experience
A configuration management procedure for the portal
A.why: Tailored end-user training, supplemented with manuals, quick-start guides and video tutorials, helps users adopt the product (14.2.1).

whyNot.1: An SLA sets operational expectations with the contractor; it does not help advisers adopt the guide.
whyNot.2: A tenant survey is a feedback loop for improvement, not support for adoption.
whyNot.3: Configuration management supports consistent maintenance, not adviser adoption.

A.q: Draycott Precision Engineering's maintenance team will own the dashboard after the project, and the software team will keep improving it. Which hand-over BEST keeps agile practices going after the transition?
options: A printed manual covering every dashboard screen
A maintenance schedule for the sensors and gateways
The product backlog, team dashboard and their tools
A list of contacts for faults at Senticore
A.why: Handing over agile artifacts and tools ensures continuity and alignment with agile practices after transition (14.2.1).

whyNot.0: A manual supports adoption, but it does not carry the agile way of working forward.
whyNot.1: A maintenance schedule supports consistent maintenance, not continuity of agile practices.
whyNot.3: Contacts form part of an escalation pathway; they do not sustain agile practices.

A.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's IT operations manager, Kieran Walsh, needs the click and collect service maintained the same way in every store and wants clear expectations of what operations will provide. What should the hand-over include?
options: A schedule of user surveys and retrospectives
Step-by-step procedures, maintenance schedules and SLAs
Quick-start guides and video tutorials for staff
The e-commerce team's product backlog and dashboard
A.why: Explicit, step-by-step operational procedures covering configuration management, maintenance schedules, SLAs and troubleshooting guides support consistent maintenance and clear expectations (14.2.1).

whyNot.0: Surveys and retrospectives are feedback loops that collect insight, not maintenance procedures.
whyNot.2: Quick-start guides and videos aid adoption by users.
whyNot.3: Handing over agile artifacts sustains agile practice; it does not define operational maintenance.

B.q: Easterholm County Council's Care Online is moving into the social care operations team. The council wants actionable insight into how carers and staff find the service, so it can keep improving it. Which transition element meets this need?
options: Escalation pathways with contacts and timelines
Service level agreements with Abacus Care Software
Quick-start guides for social workers and carers
Regular user surveys, retrospectives and check-ins
B.why: Regular feedback loops such as user surveys, retrospectives and structured check-ins collect actionable insights that drive ongoing improvement (14.2.1).

whyNot.0: Escalation pathways help resolve issues; they do not gather insight on how users find the service.
whyNot.1: SLAs define service expectations, not how users experience the service.
whyNot.2: Quick-start guides help users adopt the service rather than collecting their views.

B.q: Callowmere University's hub is live. When a fault stops bookings late in the evening, wellbeing staff do not know whom to contact or how quickly Northmere should respond. Which transition element was missing?
options: Feedback loops such as structured check-ins
Escalation pathways with contacts and timelines
Tailored end-user training for the wellbeing staff
Handing over the web team's product backlog
B.why: Escalation pathways detail points of contact and timelines for issue resolution, supporting operational handling (14.2.1).

whyNot.0: Check-ins collect insight over time; they do not say who to call when something breaks.
whyNot.2: Training helps staff use the hub, not resolve faults with the supplier.
whyNot.3: The backlog supports continued agile improvement, not urgent fault handling.

B.q: Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares project is in initiation. Project manager Rhys Pengelly sets out how the app changes will move into the customer relations team's daily use, alongside confirming people and resources and documenting the release map. Which initiating activity is this?
options: Agree the management approaches
Establish project controls
Prepare the project plan
Prepare the full business case
B.why: 'Prepare the project plan' identifies the arrangements for transition of the project product into operational use, confirms people and resources and documents the release map (Table 13.6).

whyNot.0: Agreeing the management approaches defines how change, risk, quality and the rest will be managed.
whyNot.1: Establishing controls sets stage boundaries, tolerances and escalation procedures.
whyNot.3: The full business case is a more detailed project canvas.

C.q: Draycott Precision Engineering's project is closing. Andrea Lucas plans to give the maintenance team a printed manual and to archive the product backlog and team dashboard 'to keep operations simple'. Is this an appropriate application of transition to operations guidance, and why?
options: Yes, because manuals help users to adopt the product
Yes, because the project's records close at closure
No, because artifacts and tools sustain agile practices
No, because the maintenance team should write the manual
C.why: Agile artifacts and tools should be handed over to ensure continuity and alignment with agile practices after transition (14.2.1).

whyNot.0: Manuals do help adoption, but that does not justify removing the artifacts that sustain agile ways of working.
whyNot.1: The project closes, but the product and its continued improvement do not.
whyNot.3: The verdict is right but the reason is wrong: who writes the manual is not the issue.

C.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's Release 2 is live in the 10 pilot stores. In 'evaluate stage status', Patrick Dunne confirms that the store operations team has taken ownership of the collection process in those stores. Is this an appropriate application of the processes, and why?
options: Yes, because stage status checks confirm ownership moves
Yes, because all hand-over waits for the project closure
No, because products are handed over at project closure
No, because the board confirms ownership in directing
C.why: Evaluating stage status includes confirming whether ownership of any products has been transferred to users; transition happens release by release (Table 13.9).

whyNot.1: The verdict is right but the reason is wrong: hand-over happens as releases go live, not only at closure.
whyNot.2: Products can be handed over during the project as each release goes live.
whyNot.3: Confirming ownership transfer is part of the PM's 'evaluate stage status' activity.

C.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group's new repairs service is live on the pilot estate. To find out how tenants feel about it, Sally Greaves relies on the service level agreement agreed with Coastline. Is this an appropriate application of transition to operations guidance, and why?
options: Yes, because SLAs set clear operational expectations
Yes, because Coastline employs the repair engineers
No, because SLAs are agreed after the project closes
No, because surveys and check-ins give user insight
C.why: Feedback loops such as user surveys, retrospectives and structured check-ins collect actionable insights; SLAs set operational expectations rather than measure how users feel (14.2.1).

whyNot.0: SLAs do set operational expectations, but they do not tell Sally how tenants experience the service.
whyNot.1: Coastline does employ the engineers, but that does not make its SLA a source of tenant insight.
whyNot.2: The verdict is right but the reason is wrong: SLAs form part of the operational procedures handed over.

reteach.title: Handing over a community garden
reteach.question: A volunteer group built a community garden and now hands it to the residents' association. What does the association need so the garden thrives?

blocks.h: Tools, know-how, rules, contacts and a suggestion box
blocks.body: The volunteers hand over their planting board and tools so the same way of working carries on. They run a short session and leave a one-page guide for new gardeners. They write the watering and pruning rota, list who to call if the water supply fails and how soon, and set up a monthly chat to hear what residents want next.

blocks.text: The rota keeps the garden tidy, but it will not tell you what residents want. Insight comes from the feedback loop.

explain.body: To ensure continuity and alignment with agile practices after transition, the agile artifacts and tools used during the project, such as backlogs and dashboards, should be handed over effectively.

test.q: Callowmere University's web team will keep improving the hub after the project, working with the wellbeing service. What does the transition guidance say should be handed over to keep the agile way of working going?
options: The project's agile artifacts and tools
The end project report and lessons report
A full set of user manuals and videos
The service level agreements with Northmere
test.why: Handing over agile artifacts and tools ensures continuity and alignment with agile practices after transition (14.2.1).

whyNot.1: These reports close the project; they do not carry agile practice into operations.
whyNot.2: Manuals and videos help users adopt the product.
whyNot.3: SLAs set operational expectations, not agile ways of working.

explain.body: Tailored end-user training sessions, supported by manuals, quick-start guides and video tutorials, help users adopt the product.

test.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's store staff in 85 stores must start using the collection process. What is the main purpose of giving them quick-start guides and short videos?
options: To collect insight for improvement
To set clear service levels
To help staff adopt the process
To route faults to the right team
test.why: Training supplemented with manuals, quick-start guides and video tutorials facilitates user adoption (14.2.1).

whyNot.0: Insight comes from feedback loops such as surveys and check-ins.
whyNot.1: Service levels are set in SLAs within operational procedures.
whyNot.3: Routing faults is the job of escalation pathways.

explain.body: Explicit step-by-step procedures (configuration management, maintenance schedules, SLAs, troubleshooting guides) support consistent maintenance and clear expectations. Escalation pathways add points of contact and timelines for resolving issues.

test.q: Easterholm County Council's operations team receives a document naming who to contact at Abacus when case data stops flowing, and how quickly each type of fault must be resolved. Which transition element is this?
options: Operational procedures
End-user training
Feedback loops
Escalation pathways
test.why: Escalation pathways detail points of contact and timelines for issue resolution (14.2.1).

whyNot.0: Operational procedures cover routine running and maintenance, such as schedules and troubleshooting guides.
whyNot.1: Training helps users adopt the service.
whyNot.2: Feedback loops collect insight for improvement.

explain.body: Regular feedback loops, such as user surveys, retrospectives and structured check-ins, collect actionable insights that drive ongoing improvement and show how well the product is being integrated.

test.q: Larkspur Rail's customer relations team now runs the automatic compensation service. Which arrangement will BEST give the team actionable insight into how to improve it?
options: A step-by-step troubleshooting guide
Passenger surveys and team check-ins
A contact list with response timelines
Video tutorials for new staff members
test.why: Feedback loops such as surveys, retrospectives and structured check-ins collect actionable insights for ongoing improvement (14.2.1).

whyNot.0: A troubleshooting guide supports consistent maintenance, not insight.
whyNot.2: A contact list with timelines is an escalation pathway.
whyNot.3: Video tutorials support adoption by new users.
